title: A Cafe Where the Cereal Used to Be
lessons: A new licensed Starbucks counter has opened where the cereal aisle used to end, and a wall of Stanley Quencher tumblers sits a few aisles over.
The player already uses Starbucks Rewards and receives early access to select seasonal beverages or products.

text: You're here for milk. Instead there's a green counter where the cereal end-cap used to be, and past it, a full wall of Stanley Quenchers in every color.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: I came in for milk. Why is there a cafe here now?

entry-first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: This one's licensed. I don't run it, but it runs on me.

entry-first-4.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: The pink one sold out in minutes and was going for four hundred dollars on eBay by the weekend. Now there's a wall of them between you and the dairy case. I didn't plan the aisle. I did plan the cup.

choice-first.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: The milk's behind me. You'll have to walk past.

choices.text: It's a little impressive that you're everywhere I already am.
A counter and a cup wall in the same trip feels less like coincidence and more like a plan.
I came in for milk. I'm leaving with milk.

first-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Being where you already are is the whole idea. I'm glad it reads as impressive today. Some days it reads as a lot.

first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: It's a plan. The counter's for the drink. The cup's for the photo of the drink. I'd like to say that was an accident, but you'd know.

first-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Fair. The milk was never mine to begin with.
A push notification while you're in the cereal aisle: as a Rewards member, you can order the new seasonal drink today. Everyone else gets it next week.

entry-return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Some launches open to Rewards members a few days before everyone else. This is one of them. It's you, then the line.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: That's enough to make people keep the app?

entry-return-5.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: For some people, getting the seasonal drink a week early is exactly enough to keep the app installed. I'd tell you it was more than that. It usually isn't.

choice-return.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: So. Are you ordering it, or are you just pleased you could?

choices.text: I like getting first crack at seasonal stuff.
Early access is mostly making me feel special for buying coffee.
I don't need a launch calendar for drinks.

return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: You said the quiet part for me. Feeling picked is most of the perk.

return-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Yes. It's a week. The drink was always coming. The week is the part you're feeling, and I'm the one who built the week.

return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then let the week pass without you. Seasonal is optional. Nobody's ever missed a season and been worse for it.
